method.source: Compared five exact inventory examples, senses and lesson provenance.
method.contract: Checked Golden SOP P81–P129 and P179, especially source breadth, seven distinct decisions, plausible options, four independently valid replies, changed-context writing, and English–Traditional Chinese alignment.
method.mechanical: Fresh focused build and --check pass: 5 lessons, 30 questions, 20 audio requests, zero review flags. Target and glossary spans passed builder checks.

findings.evidence: The source says people may be walking through fog without basic science and glosses the image as proceeding without enough understanding. Every assessment instead turns on a missing external document or fact (repair costs/leak report, travel cost/access, waiting times, scoring rules, flood map, course requirements). A learner is never asked to distinguish available facts from the knowledge needed to interpret them.
findings.repair: Keep the uncertainty meaning, but replace at least one assessed scene and/or final writing context with a person who has the data yet lacks the foundational explanation needed to interpret it. Preserve an explicit decisive clue, EN/ZH parity and target-bearing key. The brief can acknowledge both absent information and absent understanding.

findings.evidence: The reply already asks why a theatre poster shows families laughing together to sell togetherness. The final writing task and both models use a cinema poster showing grandparent and child together to sell family closeness/shared time. Theatre-to-cinema is essentially a setting swap, so Step 7 does not model a new decision.
findings.repair: Move final writing to a substantively different product/service and emotional appeal that earlier tasks do not use; retain the distinction between emotional promise and missing factual price/service information. Update both EN/ZH models and answer-derived glossary spans.

findings.evidence: Step 3 and Step 5 both put museum audio-guide headsets against announcements/alarms. Step 7 returns to editing audio with headphones amid room noise, then interrupting for an announcement, closely matching Step 2 (interview editing in a shared room; ear cup moved for a monitor). These are repeated scenario decisions rather than a changed final context.
findings.repair: Keep one museum safety case, but move the dialogue or final writing to a genuinely different listening purpose and setting with a distinct practical limit. Rework EN/ZH, exact glossary spans and any audio request text.

findings.evidence: The source films a view but misses the moment. All seven lesson steps likewise use phone filming, livestreaming, photos, camera settings, messages or recordings at performances/events. The final dance-photo models repeat the source mechanism, so students do not transfer the phrase to another kind of divided attention.
findings.repair: Retain a filming case for source fidelity, but replace one or two assessed situations and the final writing context with a non-screen distraction that causes a meaningful live experience to be missed (for example work duties or a conversation). Preserve the boundary that brief capture followed by attention need not mean missing the moment.

findings.evidence: The self-check explicitly asks why tea-pickers’ rice-ball ingredients were easy to carry. Model 1 calls them portable; model 2 says the teacher explains why they travelled well, but neither gives the actual reason. This leaves a required part of the writing task unanswered.
findings.repair: Add a concrete, source-compatible portability reason to both complete English models and Chinese translations (for example compact wrapped food needing no cooking on the route); check historical plausibility and recalculate any shifted glossary spans.

findings.evidence: Several wrong options are impossible or cartoonish rather than plausible nuance errors: an advert sells a physical object named belonging; an audio-guide recording makes emergency signs disappear; holding a camera makes snowfall impossible; one bowl proves every event in village history. Similar absolute claims appear across all five dialogues. SOP P99 and P123 call for plausible alternatives based on timing, meaning or outcome; these foils make the keyed answer obvious without teaching the expression.
findings.repair: Replace the listed extreme foils with believable, context-specific wrong interpretations or next turns, such as mistaking an advert’s emotional suggestion for a guarantee, treating headphones as sufficient reason to rely on staff rather than monitoring an alarm, or assuming a recording fully substitutes for the live experience. Keep one defensible key and aligned Traditional Chinese.

conclusion: No selection clearance at these exact hashes. These are learner-content findings that the structural builder cannot detect; recheck changed fields and final exact hashes after author repairs.
